newsitem.title: USA: Rising dlr helps, hurts U.S. economy - Fed's Rivlin.
newsitem.headline: Rising dlr helps, hurts U.S. economy - Fed's Rivlin.

text.p: The rising dollar has both helped and hurt the U.S. economy, Federal Reserve Vice Chair Alice Rivlin said on Thursday.
"The dollar cuts in both ways," she told a meeting of the Economic Strategy Institute.
It has helped "a lot" to keep down inflation. "It's one of the reasons that inflation clearly has been as benign as it's been," she said.
But exporters on the other hand are worried about the future of the dollar, Rivlin said.
Turning to the domestic economy, Rivlin said the United States is seeing broad-based, but not run-away, wage rises.
"We are getting pretty broad-based wage increases," she said. But she added, "They aren't run-away wage increases."

The Federal Reserve raised interest rates last month in a move that Rivlin described as a "bit of insurance" to guard against economic overheating. The move sparked criticism from both Democratic and Republican lawmakers.
Rivlin though brushed aside concerns that Congress would act to rein in the Fed's independence. "I doubt that the Congress really wants to make monetary policy. It's too hard."
